### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/knowledge-turso`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx`  _(via source_id (literal, a string literal in GENERATION_COLUMNS))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via source_id (literal, a string literal in GENERATION_COLUMNS))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via source_id (literal, a string literal in GENERATION_COLUMNS))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via beginBuild (symbol, a method of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter), completeBuild (symbol, a method of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter), dropSource (symbol, a method of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 49 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8a2749bee464f165e4d47412dac1acd3e27932db` — the merge of head `e052afa1befa37e03fd34d02a8aa10f3f84ff890` into base `4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8a2749bee464f165e4d47412dac1acd3e27932db && git checkout 8a2749bee464f165e4d47412dac1acd3e27932db
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49 e052afa1befa37e03fd34d02a8aa10f3f84ff890 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49 && git merge --no-ff e052afa1befa37e03fd34d02a8aa10f3f84ff890

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4af32b99db078cef6b9cbda8f2f4a77632b75f49` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `e052afa1befa37e03fd34d02a8aa10f3f84ff890` (Fixes #37956). Full read · 2026-11-27T16:27Z

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.** 6 files, +211/-15. Check-runs at e052afa1: 40 success, 15 expected skip, 0 failed. Mergeable state is clean. Not governed. `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`. `l1-face` is CLEAN on 13 items. No contract review is owed: there is no narrowing, and the refusal uses the `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` / 503 shape the store already answers when it is not ready.

**What I read myself.**
- **The three DROPs.** The card names `beginBuild` (:625), `completeBuild` (:652) and `dropSource` (:694). Each now goes through `dropGenerationTable`, which reads the shape with the same `shapeOf` / `tableShape` that `openGeneration` uses. It drops only `none` or `passage`, and refuses anything else inside the caller's write transaction, so the refusal rolls back the row DELETEs too. The two `legacyTable` DROPs keep their existing `hasLegacy` guard, as the card says they should.
- **`openGeneration`.** The guard moves from `legacy || other` to "not `none` and not `passage`". It now also refuses the new `generation` shape, which is right: a table with the generation table's columns is never a passage table.
- **`ready()`.** The shape of `knowledge_generation` is read before `generationDdl`, so a foreign table never gets the two unique indexes. `GENERATION_COLUMNS` equals the eight columns `generationDdl` creates, compared sorted. I checked the upgrade path. The generation table first shipped in `19.0.0-next.0` with all eight columns, including `recipe_hash`, and there is no ALTER in the DDL. The 6.x releases from the cloud repo had no generation table, only `legacy` passage tables. So no store written by an earlier release is turned away by the new check.
- **Tests.** The six acceptance cases cover each card acceptance line on both `:memory:` and a `file:` URL. An object table survives `beginBuild`, `completeBuild` and `dropSource`, each refusal names the table, and the generation rows and the served search are unchanged. Own tables are still dropped. A foreign `knowledge_generation` gives `healthCheck` `ok: false`, its rows are kept, and no index is added to it. A second adapter adopts the store's own `knowledge_generation`.
- **Prose.** The changeset, README and `knowledge.mdx` are true sentence by sentence against the code, including "nothing of the call is removed" (rollback) and "a table of the package's earlier releases is still dropped by the first complete reindex" (the `legacy` path is untouched).
- **Point (1).** Local typecheck was NOT MEASURED because the lock was never acquired. CI TypeScript Type Check is green at this head, and I take that.
- **Point (2).** I agree it is not owed. Reads and writes into a generation table go by a name the store made after `openGeneration` checked it. A foreign table can sit there only if someone swaps it in by hand afterwards. An object table made first is caught by `openGeneration`.

**Landing:** not governed, so the area lands it after ACCEPT.
